message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t give you the exact AQI value for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do to find the current status:

| Source | How to check | Typical AQI categories |
|--------|--------------|------------------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles, CA” or use the map. | 0–50 = Good, 51–100 = Moderate, 101–150 = Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, 151–200 = Unhealthy, 201–300 = Very Unhealthy, 301+ = Hazardous |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. | Same categories as above, plus a color scale. |
| **Weather Apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | Search “Los Angeles” and look for the “Air Quality” widget. | Usually shows AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **Local News** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their weather or environment sections; they often post live updates during smog events. | |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, you can open one of those sites or apps and you’ll see the current AQI, the main pollutants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and any health advisories.

---

### Quick Tips for Interpreting the AQI

| AQI Range | Health Impact | Recommended Action |
|-----------|---------------|--------------------|
| 0–50 (Good) | No adverse health effects | Normal outdoor activities |
| 51–100 (Moderate) | Sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory issues) may experience mild symptoms | Reduce prolonged outdoor exertion |
| 101–150 (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups) | Respiratory irritation, eye irritation | Limit outdoor activity, especially for sensitive groups |
| 151–200 (Unhealthy) | Everyone may experience health effects | Avoid outdoor exertion, consider indoor activities |
| 201–300 (Very Unhealthy) | Serious health effects | Stay indoors, use air purifiers, avoid outdoor exercise |
| 301+ (Hazardous) | Extremely hazardous | Stay indoors, keep windows closed, use HEPA filters |

---

### If You Need a Real‑Time API

If you’re building an app or want programmatic access, you can use the **AirNow API** (requires an API key) or the **AQICN API**. Here’s a quick example of how you might query the AQICN API in Python:

```python
import requests

city = "Los Angeles"
api_token = "YOUR_AQICN_TOKEN"

url = f"https://api.waqi.info/feed/{city}/?token={api_token}"
response = requests.get(url)
data = response.json()

if data["status"] == "ok":
    aqi = data["data"]["aqi"]
    print(f"Current AQI in {city}: {aqi}")
else:
    print("Error fetching data:", data["data"])
```

Replace `"YOUR_AQICN_TOKEN"` with your actual token. The API will return the current AQI, pollutant concentrations, and a timestamp.

---

Let me know if you’d like more details on how to interpret specific pollutants or how to set up alerts for when the AQI crosses certain thresholds!
